sentences.text:
Opposite Parties
 Mr. S.P. Das, Asc
 Mr. A.K Sarangi, Advocate
 (Informant)
 Coram: Justice V. Narasingh
 Order
10.04.2025 Order No.
04. 1.
Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner, learned counsel for the State and learned counsel for the Informant.

2. The Petitioner is seeking pre-arrest bail in connection with G.R. Case No.2618 of 2024 pending in the Court of learned S.D.J.M, Berhampur, arising out of Bada Bazar P.S. Case No.423 of 2024 for commission of offence punishable under Sections 294/420/467/468/506 IPC.
3.

It is submitted by the learned counsel that the even if the entire allegation of the prosecution is accepted at its face value, it is indicated that the Informant had made investment in sanitary business and in the process to repay the same he had issued cheque but the same was dishonoured for which the present FIR has been filed.
Hence, taking into account the nature of allegation which is primarily based on documentary evidence custodial interrogation is not necessary.
4. Learned counsels for the Informant opposes such prayer and submits that from the very inception the Petitioner had intention to cheat.
Since it is an economic offence, no leniency ought to have been shown to the Petitioner.
5. Learned counsel for the State also reiterates such submission.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is apt to note here that by order dated 18.03.2025 this Court had specifically requested the learned counsel for the Informant to place on record as to whether any proceeding under the N.I Act has been initiated on account of dishonor of cheque.
Learned counsel for the Informant submits that no such proceeding has been initiated.

7. Taking into account the nature of allegation and the background in which the same has been leveled and so far as money transaction is concerned it is inter se between the parties, it is directed that on surrendering within three weeks hence and moving for bail, the Petitioner shall be released on bail by the learned Court in seisin on such terms as deemed just and proper subject to verification of criminal antecedents of any nature.

If it comes to fore that the Petitioner has any criminal antecedents, this order shall not be given effect to.
8.
Before releasing learned Court in seisin shall also verify as to whether the order of this Court has been assailed before the Apex Court and if so, the result thereof.
9. Accordingly, the ABLAPL stands disposed of.
(V. NARASINGH) Judge PKS Signed by: PRADEEP KUMAR SWAIN
